title: 2025 PB #38: Which Of The Following Statements About

solution.summary: When a conductor is charged, the free charges within it redistribute themselves until the electric field inside the conductor is zero.

title: 2023 PB #50: An Electron E Is Moving And
content: An electron (e-) is moving and has kinetic energy of 1.00 MeV. It makes a head-on collision with a positron (e+) that is at rest. In the collision the two particles annihilate each other and are replaced by two photons (γ ) of equal energy, each traveling at angles θ to the electron's original direction of motion. The reaction is e- + e+ → 2γ. Determine the angle of emission θ of each photon.
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing momentum & collisions.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: The moving electron has momentum, p, along the positive x-axis and kinetic energy, K.
steps: 1. The moving electron has momentum, p, along the positive x-axis and kinetic energy, K.
2. The total energy, E, of the electron and the stationary positron before the collision is E = K + 2mc2 = 2.022 MeV.
3. The two photons emerge from the collision each with energy Eγ = ½ E = 1.011 MeV as given by conservation of energy, and each with magnitude of momentum pγ = Eγ/c = 1.011 MeV/c.
4. The momentum vectors of the photons make angles ±θ with the x-axis.
5. Conservation of momentum in the x-direction is p = 2pγ cos θ from which θ = 45.3o.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Momentum & Collisions problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

2. Therefore, the potential at the junction between the 100  resistor and the 300  resistor is the same as the potential at the junction between the 400  resistor and the 200  resistor.
3. As a result, the 100 ohm and 400 ohm resistors can be treated as a parallel combination connected in series to the parallel combination of the 300  and 200  resistors.
4. This gives an equivalent resistance of 200  and a total current of 60 mA.

5. The potential difference across the top two resistors must be equal and their total current must add to 60 mA, resulting in a currents of 48 mA and 12 mA in the 100  and 400  resistors, respectively.
6. Using the same reasoning, the currents in the 300  and 400  resistors are 24 mA and 36 mA, respectively.
7. Using the junction to the left of the capacitor: I100 = Ix + I300, 48 mA = 24 mA + Ix.
8. Ix = 24 mA

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing circuits & electricity.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: At steady‐state, no charge flows to or from the capacitor, so any current through the 100  resistor continues to the 300  resistor.
steps: 1. At steady‐state, no charge flows to or from the capacitor, so any current through the 100  resistor continues to the 300  resistor.
2. The same is true for the 400  resistor and the 200  resistor.
3. The potential drops across the 100  and 300  resistor must total 12 V.
4. Because the current is the same in these resistors, the voltage drops are proportional to the resistances: 3 V for the 100  and 9 V for the 300 .
5. By the same reasoning, the voltage drops across the 400 ohm and 200 ohm are 8 V and 4 V respectively.
6. The resulting potential difference between the junction to the left of the capacitor and the junction to the right of the capacitor is 5 V.
7. Using Q = CΔV = (15 μF)(5 V), gives 75 μC.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Circuits & Electricity problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

solution.summary: … Since the object is rolling without slipping, any friction would have to be static on the incline (there is no relative motion between cylinder and surface).
steps: 1. … Since the object is rolling without slipping, any friction would have to be static on the incline (there is no relative motion between cylinder and surface).

2. As for the direction, one notes that if the friction acts down the incline (as one might suspect being "opposite to the motion"), this would cause the speed of the object to decrease, but it also would cause an increase in the rotational speed of the object.
3. The torque from the center of the cylinder would make the object spin faster and faster which cannot happen.
4. Consequently, in order to slow the rotation, the friction must be pointing up the incline!

title: 2017 PB #33: Two Long Wires Are Fixed In
content: Two long wires are fixed in space so that the conventional current in the left wire (2 A) comes out of the plane of the page and the conventional current in the right wire (3 A) goes into the plane of the page. In which Region(s) is there a place on the x-axis (aside from infinity) at which the magnetic field is equal to zero from these currents?

options.text: In both Regions I and II
In both Regions I and III
In both Regions II and III

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing circuits & electricity.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: … From the right-hand rule, the thumb points along the direction of current and the right fingers wrap in the sense of the magnetic field lines.
steps: 1. … From the right-hand rule, the thumb points along the direction of current and the right fingers wrap in the sense of the magnetic field lines.
2. Consequently, for the 2-A current, the field points downward anywhere to the left of the wire and upward anywhere to the right of the wire on the x-axis.
3. Likewise, the 3-A current produces fields that point downward anywhere to the right of the wire and upward everywhere to the left of the wire.
4. To have no total field, the individual magnetic fields must cancel (point in opposite directions) and that only occurs in Regions I and III.
5. However, since points in Region III always are closer to the larger current, there is no way for the smaller current, acting from further away, to cancel the field from the larger current.
6. The only way the fields can cancel is if the larger current is acting from a greater distance which corresponds to a location in Region I.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Circuits & Electricity problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2016 PB #24: A Proton Moves With Constant Nonzero

3. By the right-hand rule, with the velocity up the plane of the page and the field into the place, the magnetic force is directed to the left.

title: 2016 PB #32: A Mass Connected To A String
content: A mass connected to a string forms a simple pendulum. The mass is released from rest and undergoes simple harmonic motion. Which one of the following choices correctly ranks the magnitude of the tension in the string (T), the gravitational force on the mass (W), and the net force acting on the mass (F) when the mass swings through its lowest point? (A) F < W = T (D) F < W < T (B) W < T < F (E) More information is required to answer the question. (C) W < F = T Divisions 1 & 2 8 Divisions 1 & 2
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing work & energy.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: … Since the mass is in simple harmonic motion, the angle from the vertical upon first release would be fairly small (< 15°).
steps: 1. … Since the mass is in simple harmonic motion, the angle from the vertical upon first release would be fairly small (< 15°).
2. When the mass swings through its lowest location, the acceleration of the mass would be straight up to the pivot of the pendulum.
3. This means that T > W to have more upward force compared to downward force.
4. To check on the size of the net force, let us assume that it is equal to the gravitational force and determine the angle at which the mass is released.
5. In other words, F = W = mv2 L = mg → mv2 = mgL where L is the length of the pendulum.

6. From mechanical energy conservation during the fall of the mass to the lowest point from the highest, we write ∆KE + ∆PE = 0 → ( 1 2 mv2 - 0) + mg(-L(1 - cos 𝜃)) = 0 where 𝜃 is the maximum angle that the string makes with the vertical.
7. Using our substitution, we have 1 2 mgL - mg(L(1 - cos 𝜃)) = 0 → cos 𝜃 = 1 2 → 𝜃 = 60°.
8. In other words, since we are nowhere near that initial angle, F < W and F < W < T.

title: 2015 PB #22: Satellite 1 Makes A Circular Orbit
content: Satellite 1 makes a circular orbit around the Earth with a radius r1 = R. Satellite 2 makes a circular orbit around the Earth with a radius r2 = 2R. steps: 1. … Making the free body for each satellite and writing Newton's Second Law gives Fnet = ma → GmM r2 = ma → a = GM r2 .

title: 2015 PB #30: A Spring Scale Reads 250 When
content: A spring scale reads 2.50 N when a small solid mass hangs from it in air. The spring scale reads 1.58 N when the mass at the end of the spring is completely submerged in a container of water. Which one of the following choices best represents the density of the solid mass?
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing gravitation & celestial.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: … The free body diagram of the solid mass in the water has three forces acting … gravitational, a spring force from the scale, and a buoyant force from the water.
steps: 1. … The free body diagram of the solid mass in the water has three forces acting … gravitational, a spring force from the scale, and a buoyant force from the water.
2. Writing Newton's Second Law, we have Fnet = ma → B + T - mg = 0.
3. We have from the measurement in the air (since the buoyant force on the small mass from the air will be effectively negligible), that mg = 2.50 N.
4. Also, we have that T = 1.58 N.
5. Solving for the buoyant force yields B = 2.50 - 1.58 = 0.92 N.
6. The buoyant force is computed as 𝜌waterg V = 0.92 ⇒ V = 0.92 (1000)(10) = 9.2 x 10-5m3.
7. The mass of the object is found as m = 2.50 10 = 0.250 kg leading to a density of the mass as 𝜌 = m V = 0.250 9.2x10-5 = 2.7 x 103 kg m3

title: 2015 PB #31: Approximately How Many Hydrogen Atoms Are
content: Approximately how many hydrogen atoms are there in the liquid water of Earth's oceans?
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing modern physics & relativity.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: … Approximately 70% of the Earth's surface is water.
steps: 1. … Approximately 70% of the Earth's surface is water.

2. Approximating the volume of water with the surface area of the earth multiplied by a depth of about 3 mile (5000 meters approximately), we have Vwater = 7 10 4𝜋r2(3 mi) = 28 10 𝜋(6.4 x 106)2(5000) = 1.8 x 1018m3.
3. The density of water is 1000 kg m3 and so the total mass of water in the oceans is 1.8 x 1018 ∗ 1000 = 1.8 x 1021kg.
4. The molar mass of water is 18 g mol (H = 1, O = 16) yielding n = 1.8x1021 0.018 = 1.0 x 1023 mol.
5. There are 2 4 hydrogen atoms per water molecule, and so we need the number of molecules from Avogadro… N = nNA = (1.0 x 1023)(6.02 x 1023) = 6.0 x 1046 giving 2(6.0 x 1046) = 1.2 x 1047 H atoms.
6. *** http://water.usgs.gov/edu/earthwherewater.html is where this question was vetted.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Modern Physics & Relativity problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2015 PB #32: An Object Moving Along A Line
content: An object moving along a line completes a 20.0 second trip with an average speed of 10.0 m s⁄ in two stages. During stage 1, the object moves with a constant velocity of 6.0 m s⁄ to the right for 12.0 seconds. What constant magnitude acceleration directed to the left must the object have during the 8.0 seconds of stage 2?
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing kinematics.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: … For the average speed to be 10 m s , a total distance of 200 m must be traveled.
steps: 1. … For the average speed to be 10 m s , a total distance of 200 m must be traveled.
2. In the first 12 seconds, a total of ∆x = 〈v〉∆t = (6.0 m s ) (12s) = 72 m has been traveled.
3. This means that in the last 8 seconds, a distance of 128 m needs to be traversed.
4. Let's draw a graph of velocity vs time.
5. The shaded regions have to add to a total distance of 128 m.
6. In the first T seconds, the object slows to rest.
7. Mathematically, |a| = 6 T with area 1 2 (6)(T) = 3T.
8. For the remaining time, the area is 1 2 (8 - T)(a(8 - T)) = 1 2 a(8 - T)2.
10. Substituting the expression for the acceleration and multiplying by T yields 3T2 + 3(8 - T)2 = 128 T ⇒ 3T2 - 88T + 96 = 0.
11. Solving this expression yields times of T = 1.13 s, 28.2 s.
12. Using T = 1.13 s gives a = 6 1.13 = 5.3 m s2.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Kinematics problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2015 PB #33: Two Spherical Speakers Separated By 300
content: Two spherical speakers separated by 30.0 m each emit a constant frequency signal of 57.0 Hz in phase with each other. The speed of sound is 342 m s. How many locations of complete destructive interference of the incoming signals are there on the line between the speakers?
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing oscillations & shm.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: … The wavelength of the sounds is v = f𝜆 ⇒ 𝜆 = v f = 342 57 = 6.0 m.
steps: 1. … The wavelength of the sounds is v = f𝜆 ⇒ 𝜆 = v f = 342 57 = 6.0 m.
2. This means that the speakers are separated by exactly 5 wavelengths.
3. For constructive interference, the path difference between the waves from the speakers must differ than an integer number of wavelengths.
4. Hence, there are 11 locations at or between the speakers where this happens -5𝜆, -4𝜆, -3𝜆, … 3𝜆, 4𝜆, 5𝜆.
5. A place of destructive interference occurs directly between the constructive interference locations… hence, there are 10 of them.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Oscillations & SHM problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2015 PB #34: An Upwardpointing Object Is Placed 150
content: An upward-pointing object is placed 15.0 cm to the left of a lens system. The first lens is convex with focal length 10.0 cm. The second lens is convex with focal length 10 cm and its location from the first lens is varied from 10 cm away to 110 cm away. Which one of the following choices best represents the description of the final image formed as the second lens is moved from x = 10 cm to x = 110 cm from the first lens?

options.text: Real & pointing downward Virtual & pointing downward Real & pointing upward
Virtual & pointing downward Virtual & pointing upward Real & pointing upward
Virtual & pointing upward Virtual & pointing downward Real & pointing downward
Real & pointing upward Virtual & pointing downward Real & pointing upward
Virtual & pointing downward Real & pointing upward

hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing waves & optics.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: … The image from the first lens is found from 1 f = 1 p + 1 q → 1 10 = 1 15 + 1 q → q = 30 cm.
steps: 1. … The image from the first lens is found from 1 f = 1 p + 1 q → 1 10 = 1 15 + 1 q → q = 30 cm.

2.  Far from 1st lens (more than 40 cm from the first lens) - we have that the image from the first lens is the object for the second lens and that the object is greater than a focal length from the 2nd lens.
3. This means that we will end up with a real image from the 2nd lens and the image will be flipped from the "object".
4. Since the 1st lens formed a real image, that image was flipped from the original object.
5. In other words, for large distance between the lenses, the image is real and pointing upward.
6.  Medium range from 1st lens (between 30 and 40 cm from the 1st lens) - the image from the first lens is now inside the focal length of the 2nd lens.
7. Hence, between 30 and 40 cm, the image formed is virtual and pointing downward (there is still the inversion from the 1st lens).
8.  Close range - (less than 30 cm from the first lens) - we have a virtual object!
9. For simplicity, let the 2nd lens be placed 20 cm from the first lens making p = -10 cm for the second lens.
10. This gives 1 f = 1 p + 1 q → 1 10 = 1 -10 + 1 q → q = 5 cm.
11. Because we have a positive image position, the image is real.
12. Further, the magnification of the image from the 2nd lens is M = - q p = - ( 5 -10) = 1 2.
13. Because it is positive, the image has the same orientation as the object.
14. The object for this lens was the upside-down image from the first lens.
15. Hence, the image is real and pointing downward.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Waves & Optics problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2015 PB #36: Rain Falls Vertically At 120 Ms
content: Rain falls vertically at 12.0 m/s with respect to a stationary observer. A car is moving at an angle of 40° below the horizontal with respect to the observer. A passenger sitting in the car notes that the rain makes an angle of 29.0° with the vertical. What is the car's speed with respect to the observer?
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing kinematics.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: … METHOD #1: algebra - One way to handle this problem is to make little pictures and use subscripts.
steps: 1. … METHOD #1: algebra - One way to handle this problem is to make little pictures and use subscripts.
2. We write v⃗rain wrt Eartℎ = (0)x̂ + (-12)ŷ, v⃗car wrt Eartℎ = (vcar cos 40)x̂ + (-vcar sin 40)ŷ = (0.776 vcar)x̂ + (-0.643 vcar)ŷ.
3. Now, to find the velocity of the rain with respect to the car, we compute v⃗rain wrt car + v⃗car wrt Eartℎ = v⃗rain wrt Eartℎ.
4. Hence, we rearrange this expression to find v⃗rain wrt car = v⃗rain wrt Eartℎ - v⃗car wrt Eartℎ = (0 - 0.776 vcar)x̂ + (-12 + 0.643 vcar)ŷ.
5. Since these components of the velocity are known to make a 29 degree angle 5 with the vertical, we can write tan 290 = (-0.776 vcar) -12+0.643vcar .
6. Using a little algebra, we can solve this equation for the unknown vcar.
7. Doing this leads to vcar = 5.93 m s .
8. METHOD #2: pictorial - Using v⃗rain wrt car + v⃗car wrt Eartℎ = v⃗rain wrt Eartℎ, we construct the picture shown to the right for the velocities.
9. Hence, from the Law of Sines, 12 sin 101 = vcar sin 29 ⇒ vcar = 12 sin 29° sin 101° = 5.93 m s
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Kinematics problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2015 PB #38: A Thin Film Of Alcohol 135
content: A thin film of alcohol (nalcoℎol = 1.35) lies on a flat glass surface (nglass = 1.60). When light of wavelength 540 nm is incident normal to the alcohol surface from air, the light is strongly reflected, but when light of wavelength 432 nm is incident normal to the surface from air, the reflected light is minimized. Which one of the following choices could represent the thickness, t, of the alcohol film?
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing waves & optics.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: … To create constructive interference with the 540 nm light, we need to be sure that the interfering rays from the reflection off the alcohol and the ray that passes into the alcohol and is reflected back at the glass surface are in phase.
steps: 1. … To create constructive interference with the 540 nm light, we need to be sure that the interfering rays from the reflection off the alcohol and the ray that passes into the alcohol and is reflected back at the glass surface are in phase.
2. Since the light is traveling from air to alcohol to glass, the index of refraction increases at each interface, meaning that the reflected light is phase-shifted by 𝜆 2.

3. This means that for light traveling down through the alcohol a distance t to the glass surface and then traveling an additional distance t back to the air, we need this extra path length to be an integer number of wavelengths to put the our two waves in phase.
4. That is, 2t = m 𝜆 n.
5. Solving for t = m𝜆 2n = m ( 540 (2)(1.35)) = 200 m.
6. Since m is an integer, the only possible choice would be t = 400 nm.
7. Likewise, destructive interference is needed for the 432 nm light and that condition is2t = (p + 1 2) 𝜆 n.
8. Solving this expression with p = 2 also yields that t = 400 nm.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Waves & Optics problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2015 PB #45: A 600 Parallelplate Capacitor Is Disconnected
content: A 6.00 𝜇F parallel-plate capacitor is disconnected from a 12 volt battery after being fully charged. A person now carefully inserts a dielectric material of constant 𝜅 = 2 so that it fills one-half of the space between the plates as shown. How much work was done by the person while inserting the dielectric?
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing circuits & electricity.
Check relevant reference formulas and standard sign conventions.

solution.summary: … The work done by the person inserting the dielectric would be equal to the change in the potential energy for the capacitor.
steps: 1. … The work done by the person inserting the dielectric would be equal to the change in the potential energy for the capacitor.
2. Since the battery was disconnected, the charge on the plates remains constant and Wperson = ∆U = 1 2 Q∆V.
3. The charge on the plates would be Q = CV = (6.00 𝜇F)(12.0 v) = 72.0 𝜇C.
4. The final capacitance can be found by moving the dielectric to any location in the space between plates and treating the system as 2 capacitors in series.
5. The potential difference through the air-filled portion would be 6 volts since the field strength is unchanged and we are crossing half the original capacitor (which had 12 volts).

6. For the dielectric portion, the dielectric decreases the field strength by a factor of 2… which means that the potential difference across the dielectric would be 3 volts for a grand total of 9 volts across the entire capacitor.
7. Hence, Wperson = 1 2 Q∆V = 1 2 (72𝜇C)(-3v) = -108 𝜇J.
solution.keyTakeaway: Fundamental principle: Circuits & Electricity problem solving for AAPT PhysicsBowl.

title: 2015 PB #48: Two Concentric Charged Conducting Shells Are
content: Two concentric charged conducting shells are in free space. The outer shell has inner radius 2a and outer radius 3a. The inner shell has radius a. It is known that the electric potential at r = 3a is V3a = kQ 3a⁄. If the electric potential Va at r = a is 0 volts, what is the charge on the inner spherical shell, Qin?
hints: Identify the core physics concepts governing circuits & electricity.

solution.summary: … Outside the shell of radius 3a, the total field will be that of a point charge and so will the potential giving V3a = kQ 3a.
steps: 1. … Outside the shell of radius 3a, the total field will be that of a point charge and so will the potential giving V3a = kQ 3a.

2. Between 2a and 3a, there is no field interior to the conductor (since the shells are in free space and there is no mention of any other charges nearby… the system quickly attains static equilibrium) and so the potential at 2a is given as V2a = kQ 3a.

3. Noting that there is a field between a and 2a, we have a potential difference computed as ∆V = Vf - Vi where Vf = Va and Vi = V2a and on the left side we write ∆V = V(r) - V(2a) = kQin a - kQin 2a .
4. And so, we have kQin a - kQin 2a = 0 - kQ 3a.
5. This leads to kQin 2a = - kQ 3a ⇒ Qin = - 2 3 Q

solution.summary: … METHOD #1: The free body diagram will have a gravitational force, a normal force, and a friction force acting.

2. By writing those forces into components and noting that there is no acceleration, we have Fnetx = max ⇒ mg sin 𝜃 - fs = 0 and Fnety = may ⇒ n - mg cos 𝜃 = 0 .
3. By solving for the normal force and the friction force, we take the ratio and obtain fs n = mg sin 𝜃 mg cos 𝜃 = tan 𝜃 ⇒ 𝜃 = tan-1 ( 38 62) = 31.5°.
4. Finally, using either expression from Newton's Law, we find the mass as m = fs g sin 𝜃 = 38 10 sin 31.5° = 7.27 kg.
5. METHOD #2: Noting that the object is in static equilibrium, the sum of the vector forces is equal to zero.
6. This means that the sum of the normal and friction forces must be equal and opposite to the gravitational force.

8. The size of the force can be found from the Pythagorean Theorem, since the normal and friction forces are at right angles to each other, to give mg = √(38)2 + (62)2 = 72.7 N.
